notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-7b31c4, issue #1210, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by Claude Code, session cc-39fac3 (issue #1209) - a different session, as the job requires.

Sources. Both recorded hashes reproduce byte for byte: the arXiv v1 PDF 3e2736beea70ba3467ad30a24b518d82cf589d9ddd4a06f6b0684c7bfd7d6306 and, more usefully, the LaTeX e-print e18e82663000a365452b439e971bb49d05a7ea6ce03201309166120e30a44c9e (ReidemeisterPaperArxiv.tex, 10889 lines). Every check below was therefore made against the authors' own source and each verdict cites a TeX line. The published Inventiones text (123 pp.) is paywalled and was not read, as the extraction states; all locators are arXiv v1 pages and statement numbers. I rebuilt the numbering from the source - Theorem, Proposition, Remark and Example are numbered by section, Lemma and Definition by subsection, equations by section - and every statement the extraction cites lands on an environment of the right kind.

Findings. All 25 sourceIssues now carry verdicts and all 25 are confirmed: 17 misprints, 6 errors and 2 gaps. For each I located the printed text in the LaTeX and checked the correction; where the correction is a computation I redid it.

Three matter. E3 and E4 together are the substantial finding, and I confirm them: Lemma 2.7.1 asserts that Sp_{2r}(F_q) and SL_{2r}(F_q) have vanishing integral H_2 for odd q, but the Schur multiplier of the universal Chevalley group A_1(q) is nontrivial exactly for q = 4 and q = 9, and SL_2(9) = 2.A_6 has H_2 = Z/3 because the universal central extension of A_6 is 6.A_6. Nothing is lost in Lemma 2.7.1 itself, which needs only H_2/2 = 0. The consequence is in Lemma 5.1.1, which deduces irreducibility of the geometric fibre of the Hurwitz stack from Dunfield-Thurston 'since H_2(G,Z) is trivial in the case at hand', with G = Sp_{2r}(ell) for an arbitrary finite field ell of characteristic other than 2 and p. For r = 1 and #ell = 9 the fibre has at least three components, by the Livingston/Dunfield-Thurston classification of mapping class group orbits by the invariant in H_2(G,Z) that the proof itself invokes. That case is inside Theorem 3.1 - 9 is 1 mod 8, as the hypothesis requires - and it is not empty: q = 73 is 1 mod 8, prime to #SL_2(F_9) = 720, and a square in the prime field F_3. So the proof of step (A), and with it Theorem 3.1, does not cover r = 1, #ell = 9. E25 is the second: the corollary (1.5) of the topological theorem is used in the proof of Lemma 5.2.1 for local systems with coefficients in the finite field ell, while the chain that proves it - Lemma C.2.1 and the circle formula (B.30) - assumes characteristic zero, through Jacobson-Morozov and the logarithm M = -log(A); section 2.3.2 says as much ('true when the characteristic of K is zero, and likely holds in general'). E19 is the third: the base-change compatibility asserted in Appendix B.10 holds for the normalized class, not for RT. I verified this myself rather than relying on the computer calculation the extraction reports, using the paper's own formula (B.30): for V = H + H over Q[s]_(s) with A_s = diag(1+s,(1+s)^{-1}) on the first plane and the identity on the second, RT = -(1+s) generically (h = 2) and RT = 1 at s = 0 (h = 4), while the specialization of -(1+s) is -1, a nonsquare. The discrepancy is exactly the normalizing sign (-1)^{chi_{1/2}/2} of Theorem 2.2, so the printed claim that the sign depends 'only on the dimension data of the complexes' is too weak: it depends on the rank of the middle differential, which jumps under specialization. My witness is orthogonal, and B.10 restricts to skew-symmetric rho with k even while saying the other case 'should be identical'; that is the limit of my check, and I say so in the verdict.

The remaining errors are local and each was checked: E7 (Pic(X) is infinite, so the displayed map is surjective rather than injective, which is all the argument needs), E12 (the skew form descends to the image of d, not to its cokernel, giving that rank d is even), E20 (delta must be the discriminant on the generalized 1-eigenspace, as Zassenhaus's formula gives; on the actual fixed space the form is degenerate when T is not semisimple), E8 (the smallest D with E >= 6N can be 1, and distinct points need not impose independent conditions on hyperplanes; Poonen's Lemma 2.1, which the paper cites, needs D >= r - 1). The misprints are all verifiable against the paper's own neighbouring text - the non-alternating form in the notation section, '4r-manifold' for a dimension divisible by 4, the epsilon-factor missing an inverse, (d) cited for what (c) says, a missing sign in Grothendieck-Lefschetz, invariants of rho where invariants of rho tensor rho are meant, 'unramified outside m' for 'at m', the degree shift in the Appendix A.7 table, four separate slips in Appendix B, the left-hand side of (B.30) for its right-hand side, chi(g) where chi is defined only on H, beta' of a class of the wrong degree, and Pic(X) for Pic(X-tilde) together with 'trivial' for 'nontrivial' in the numerical appendix.

I add no finding of my own.

Coverage. The paper has 37 numbered environments, and every one is named in an item locator or name; the remaining items carry the paper's many unnumbered statements, which is right for a paper that states most of its intermediate results in running text.

A note on the briefs, which are the best part of this extraction. Both state the final theorems with their hypotheses and numbers, and both already carry the corrections the findings imply: the Part II brief records that the proof does not cover r = 1, #ell = 9 and that Lemma 5.2.1 needs the topological corollary with finite coefficients, and the new-roadmap brief instructs that the circle formula and Lemma C.2.1 be planned in every characteristic other than 2. The design jobs should also carry E19's correction, that Appendix B.10's base change holds for the normalized class.

What this review did not do. I did not read the published version, so no finding here is checked against the version of record. I did not re-derive the paper's proofs; I read the introduction, sections 2.7, 3.1-3.3, 3.7, 3.10, 5.1-5.2, 5.5, 6.4-6.5 and Appendices A.6-A.7, B.3-B.10, C and D in the LaTeX, together with every passage a finding names. I did not redo the computer calculation behind the symplectic witness of E19, and say so in that verdict. scripts/check_paper.py and research/blueprint/intake.py check-files both pass.
